id: WIN-ID-10 (Windows pids: a lock holder's record is an MSYS pid, never read as a Windows one)
note: lock::with's owner record holds the holder's own $$, an MSYS pid under Git Bash's perl, so it is judged by MSYS rules only (identity::alive_own: kill 0 and its own /proc start), never through the winpid map or `ps -W` (identity::win_probe). A helper killed mid-lock leaves its record with a dead MSYS pid; when a live Windows process holds the same number in ps -W's WINPID column, or no listing can be read, that record must still be taken over: read as alive-unknown it was never taken over and every later save-copy (seq.lock), finish (reconcile.lock) and orphans pass died with lock-timeout until that Windows process exited. Seams STORE_TEST_OS, STORE_TEST_PROC_ROOT (a stand-in /proc), STORE_TEST_WINPIDS and STORE_TEST_PS_W: (1) a dead holder that ps -W lists is taken over (lock_stale dead); (2) the same with no ps -W listing; (3) a dead holder whose number maps, as a Windows pid, to a running MSYS pid is taken over too; (4) control: a live holder (the runner, with its stand-in /proc start) is never broken: lock-timeout; (5) the same live holder with another start is taken over (lock_stale start-time). The holder pids 999998 and 999999 are above macOS's pid range, as in AT-M5-04
